descriptor: A black-and-white bear that lives almost entirely on bamboo in the misty mountain forests of central China.

range.summary: Temperate bamboo forests between about 1,200 and 3,500 m in six mountain ranges of Sichuan, Shaanxi and Gansu.

regions.name: Minshan
regions.note: Minshan holds the most pandas; a bamboo die-off there in the mid-1970s left at least 138 dead.

regions.name: Qionglai
regions.note: Qionglai includes Wolong, where the first captive-bred panda was released into the wild in 2006.

regions.name: Qinling
regions.note: The Qinling pandas, on the northern edge of the range, are a genetically distinct population.

regions.name: Liangshan
regions.note: Liangshan is the southernmost of the six mountain ranges where wild pandas survive.

regions.name: Daxiangling
regions.note: Daxiangling holds one of the smaller, more isolated panda populations.

regions.name: Xiaoxiangling
regions.note: Tao Tao, a captive-born male, was released at Liziping here in 2012 to bolster a tiny population.

regions.name: Fengxian, west Qinling
regions.note: Unseen in Fengxian county since before the 1970s, pandas were confirmed back there in 2006.

regions.name: Hubei, Shennongjia
regions.note: Pandas still lived in Hubei into the 1800s but later vanished from the Shennongjia area.

source.label: IUCN Red List: Ailuropoda melanoleuca (Swaisgood, Wang and Wei 2016)

rangeHistory.note: Older losses across Hunan, Hubei, Guizhou and Yunnan are poorly dated; the Hubei year is approximate.

population.unit: wild giant pandas in China (national surveys)

source.label: State Forestry Administration, Fourth National Giant Panda Survey

population.note: Each point is the end year of a multi-year national survey. Methods improved over time, so early surveys are not strictly comparable. The 2014 figure excludes dependent cubs, and officials said in 2024 the wild population was nearly 1,900.

threats.title: Habitat fragmentation
threats.detail: Roads, dams and settlements split pandas into more than 30 isolated subpopulations.

threats.title: Small, isolated groups
threats.detail: Many subpopulations hold fewer than 10 animals and risk inbreeding and local loss.

threats.title: Climate change
threats.detail: Warming is projected to shrink the bamboo forests pandas rely on by over a third this century.

threats.title: Bamboo die-offs
threats.detail: Bamboo flowers and dies en masse every few decades, leaving fragmented pandas with nowhere to move.

places.name: Foping National Nature Reserve
places.note: Qinling reserve with one of the highest wild panda densities.

places.name: Tangjiahe National Nature Reserve
places.note: Minshan forests with takin, golden monkeys and occasional pandas.

places.name: Wolong National Nature Reserve
places.note: Famous panda research base in the Qionglai mountains; wild sightings are rare.

sightings.tip: Pandas move down to lower bamboo forests in winter and early spring, and March to April is the mating season, when they are most active. Even then, a wild sighting takes luck and a local tracker.

actions.title: Choose certified wood and paper
actions.detail: FSC-certified products reduce logging pressure on mountain forests.

actions.title: Support habitat corridors
actions.detail: Replanted bamboo corridors reconnect isolated groups so pandas can breed and move.

actions.title: Skip panda photo ops
actions.detail: Pay-to-hold experiences stress animals; visit reserves that put wild habitat first.

actions.title: Back long-term monitoring
actions.detail: Camera traps and DNA surveys tell rangers where pandas are and where they are vanishing.
